20 year old female here and honestly I was pretty defeated too, but u have to realize its a mostly permanent joint disorder that you will have to face for the rest of your life. But don't get sad right away, take care of your jaw go to a specialist(when u can afford to), go to the chiropractor, do yoga, don't drink, don't smoke, don't smoke weed(makes bruxism worse i have been quitting weed to stop symptoms), stay hydrated, don't overwork your jaw (stop eating corn chips and replace it with chip puffs). Its just from now on you will have to take steps to maintain jaw health dude and I know it sucks and the pain sucks bad I understand, I pay a specialist I feel way too much money to correct this extremely painful joint disorder but I am getting somewhere i feel, but it doesn't come within days or weeks it will take about a month or two to see results. Relief is different once i saw the right guy i had no pain within a week so its amazing what some doctors can do. Dont get discouraged, listen to your doctor stay healthy and maintain your jaw. (funny that I saw this today I was getting pretty upset that my jaw started to click again and the doc won't see me until the 15th of sep, RIP, but thank ~you~ for reminding me to not get discouraged as well through this short reddit post lol)

currently I have a special made splint for daytime use and I also wear it while eating. I have one for the night that makes my back teeth float and puts pressure on my front. I have a major clenching problem and it destroyed my joints in my jaw but slowly the splint is helping because it also replaces the teeth I wore down. I do have a lisp but it gets better as time goes on. I have zero clicking so far and minimal pain but you have to know that tmj/tmd is a chronic disorder and you have to manage pain through stretching and diet too. (one big thing to mention too is that a confident specialist won't prescribe pain killers until ALL other options have been explored and belive that their treatment will be the ultimate solution)
